mission: Wake the three survivors, break Ben's understanding of Jedi history in a single sentence, and get the group moving before the full history can be sorted out. The chapter should feel human first: shock, disorientation, and immediate dependency.
chapter_turn: Ben stops being an investigator with a mystery and becomes the person responsible for three witnesses out of time. He leaves the fortress with a broken version of the Order's founding story and an unnamed enemy already ahead of them.

pressure_ladder.label: hook
pressure_ladder.note: Ben and Desh enter the stasis ring and find the shape of the catastrophe in the room itself: twelve chambers, nine dead, three fading, one broken from the inside.

pressure_ladder.label: reveal
pressure_ladder.note: Sera, Torin, and Kael wake. One sentence breaks Ben's understanding of the Reformations, and the scene must let each survivor arrive as a distinct person, not a history lesson.

pressure_ladder.label: reveal
pressure_ladder.note: The group confirms that someone escaped weeks earlier and is already moving. Treat the empty chamber as a live threat, not a solved reveal.

pressure_ladder.label: decision
pressure_ladder.note: The group forms because there is no safe alternative. Ben leaves the fortress with responsibility, a direction, and far less certainty than he had when he entered.

next_scene_obligations.note: The Failing Seal — Race Against Veraine: Main dramatic throughline. The wound in the Force is real, the seal is failing, and Veraine is racing to exploit the crisis. Carries the central dramatic question: can Ben succeed where the Jedi Lords failed?
The Old War — Sera/Torin Relationship: Character depth + thematic pressure
The Conscript's Choice — Kael's Identity Arc: Thematic testing + main plot complication

The Institutional Reckoning — GAG Shadow, Reformations Cover-Up, and Veraine as the Mirror: Main plot complication + thematic pressure + Jacen parallel reinforcement. Merged per D5 — Veraine's institutional antagonism is the Order's internal politics expressed through one character, and Ben/Desh's GAG shadow is the personal register of the same question. The merged subplot carries (a) Ben and Desh's shared GAG history surfacing and being acknowledged, (b) Ben's discovery and metabolization of the Reformations' true purpose, (c) his agonizing decision to withhold from Luke under crisis conditions, (d) Veraine's parallel institutional exploitation as the mirror against which his choice is tested, and (e) his final choice to tell the Order. All five strands converge on Ch 28 s2 — the office scene pays off the thread that has been running through Veraine's ledger, Ben's silences, and Desh's steady presence all along.
Sera/Torin: dormant — thousand-year stasis, last met at Veranthos → awake and present — recognition, thousand-year ache in the body, no language yet for what's been lost
Kael/Group: non-existent — Kael has no place → adjacent — conscripted into proximity without being asked if he wanted it
Ben/Desh: operational partnership — survey team, Ch 1 dynamic → co-witnesses — both now hold the same impossible institutional fact and neither yet knows what to do with it
The Ruusan Reformations were dual-purpose — the public reform the Order remembers, and a private penance for something the Jedi Lords did.
Torin's quiet question about the modern Jedi's relationship with the light/dark boundary — 'Gavran thought so too. Before.' — seeds his eventual turn: soft
The perimeter facility message: 'the seal is failing' — coordinates to the fortress in uncharted space: soft

exit_vector.summary: The Steady Returns lifts from Gavran's fortress with six aboard. Ben at the viewport. The wrongness has a destination. The antagonist is out there, unnamed — whoever broke out from inside has a weeks-old head start. Ch 6 s1 will give the room her name.
